summary.headline: Elecon Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue fell to INR746 crore (from INR798 crore) as Gear sales dropped 21%; FY27 guidance held back.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue declined moderately YoY to INR746 crore, with EBITDA of INR158 crore (21.2% margin) and PAT of INR108 crore before a INR102 crore goodwill impairment. Gear Division revenue fell 21% YoY to INR472 crore on customer-led delivery deferrals, mainly in steel, while MHE grew 37% to INR274 crore. Management attributed the March shortfall to geopolitical-driven deferrals and said it will not give FY27 guidance, citing limited visibility. Open order book rose to about INR1,292 crore from INR948 crore a year earlier.

segments.name: Gear Division
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR472 crore (63% of consolidated) vs INR597 crore, down 21%; EBIT INR91 crore vs INR147 crore, margin about 19.3%. Q4 order intake INR550 crore; open order book INR894 crore at 31 March 2026 vs INR583 crore a year earlier.

segments.name: Material Handling Equipment (MHE)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR274 crore (37% of consolidated) vs INR200 crore, up 36.8%; EBIT INR62 crore vs INR59 crore. Q4 order inflow INR107 crore (described as a 10-quarter low); order book INR398 crore vs INR365 crore a year earlier.

guidance_outlook: No FY27 guidance; management is holding guidance and will revisit once the operating environment is clearer.
Management expects no degrowth vs FY26 in FY27; the growth rate is not quantified.
Management said that if domestic orders execute smoothly, EBITDA margin could return to the earlier 22%-24% range; no timeline given.
Sustainable MHE margin estimated at about 20%-22%.
Management said EBITDA margin should not be affected by the Gear-to-MHE mix shift in the long term.
Gear: about INR77 crore of March dispatches deferred (INR12 crore on hold, INR34 crore slipping to April, INR31 crore production put on hold); expected to clear in Q1 FY27.
Gear: a large order was described as at LOI stage and expected to convert within days; value not disclosed.
Indian Navy aircraft carrier RFP expected in Q1 FY27, orders now expected by Q4 FY27; P-17 Alpha deferred to around Q3 FY28.
capex_capacity: Capex plan of INR400 crore over FY26-FY28; about INR95 crore spent so far, with roughly 80% in Gear and the rest in MHE.
Capacity utilisation at about 56%-60% including recent capex additions.
About INR750-800 crore of capital employed sits in investments yielding about 8%; management is holding these pending clarity on expansion plans.
Established a step-down subsidiary in Mexico to serve Latin America and avoid the 50% US tariff; no significant capex planned there yet.
Four patents taken, three more under application; R&D spend continuing on new products.
demand_pricing: Export share about 18% of consolidated revenue in Q4 (domestic 82%); Middle East weakness noted, UAE overseas entity exposed to Strait of Hormuz disruption.
Q4 catalogue vs engineered mix (Gear): 55% catalogue and 45% engineered; FY26 mix 55:45 (catalogue:engineered). Management said engineered orders in hand at 31 March may execute next year.
MHE inquiry pipeline above INR1,000 crore across sectors; more than INR15 crore of orders received in April 2026.
Gear demand cited from power, steel and cement; sugar demand expected to rise on ethanol demand linked to crude supply concerns.
Input cost inflation: management said raw material was secured on order receipt and new orders are priced for higher raw material and logistics costs.
Receivables rose to about INR720 crore from about INR610 crore, with about INR70-75 crore linked to Feb-March sales not yet due and about INR15 crore overdue.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the Gear-to-MHE mix moved to 63:37 from the historical 75:25, and does it affect EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said long-term margin should not vary, with mix possibly shifting further as both divisions grow.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ROCE outlook given ROCE fell from 29% in FY24 to 20.4% in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said about INR800 crore of capital employed is in investments yielding about 8%, and only about INR95 crore of the INR400 crore capex has been spent so far. Management expects capex to lift capacity and margins over the next two years.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the goodwill impairment, and was there a tax benefit?
qa_highlights.answer: The INR102 crore impairment relates to goodwill from the 2010-11 Benzler and Radicon acquisitions, held only in consolidated accounts. The tax deduction sits with the UK entity, with about GBP1 million of claims left over about five years.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q4 gear shortfall was caused by geopolitical events in March?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the impact was concentrated in March, with about INR70 crore of dispatches affected, and the Q4 revenue guidance cut of at least 5% had been flagged in January.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins return to the earlier 22%-24% range?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it cannot commit to margin levels given the geopolitical situation, but if domestic orders execute smoothly, EBITDA margin could return to the earlier 22%-24% range.

qa_highlights.question: What are the sustainable margins for MHE?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 20%-22% is sustainable, given the revenue mix.

risks_watch: Gear deliveries: INR77 crore of March dispatches deferred; whether they clear in Q1 FY27 and whether steel-sector deferrals persist.
No FY27 guidance; FY27 revenue growth and margin trajectory unquantified.
Margin recovery depends on engineered-product orders (about 50% of open engineered orders) executing; about INR45-46 crore of finished inventory at cost awaiting invoicing.
Defence timelines have slipped (aircraft carrier RFP Q1 FY27; P-17 Alpha FY28), and Navy development orders carry lower margins (1-2 percentage points), with size not disclosed.
Middle East war and Strait of Hormuz disruption affecting the UAE subsidiary, raw material and logistics costs.
Receivables rose to about INR720 crore; overdue amounts need monitoring.
Capacity utilisation of about 56%-60% and slow deployment of the INR400 crore capex plan.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term demand but cautious on the near term: management repeatedly deferred numeric guidance and margin targets to geopolitical uncertainty, while stating that current challenges are transient. Answers on Navy margins and some margin figures were deferred or not given.
key_quotes: We believe that current challenges are transient and do not alter our long-term growth trajectory.
As previously communicated, we will not be providing forward -looking guidance for FY27.
So, we are holding our guidance for FY '27 at this stage and will revisit our outlook once there is greater clarity and stability in the operating environment.
Going forward, the EBITDA margin should not be affected.
